claims.text: A logical backup stores a database as the statements and data that rebuild it, as opposed to a copy of the server's data files (file system level backup).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: Chapter 25 Backup and Restore (25.1 SQL Dump vs 25.2 File System Level Backup); glossary entry logical-backup

claims.text: pg_dump reads one database inside one transaction whose statements all see the snapshot taken when it began (unlike Read Committed; as under Repeatable Read), so another transaction's change is wholly in the dump or wholly absent.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_dump Description; 25.1 SQL Dump ('snapshot of the database at the time pg_dump began running'); 13.2.1 Read Committed vs 13.2.2 Repeatable Read

claims.text: pg_dump --format custom (short -Fc) writes a custom-format archive that is not a plain SQL script; pg_restore reads it and can restore the whole database or only selected tables (--table).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_dump option -F/--format (c = custom); pg_restore Description and option -t/--table

claims.text: Roles (and their passwords) and tablespaces are server-wide (global) objects that pg_dump does not dump; pg_dumpall --globals-only dumps only these global objects, no databases.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_dump Notes / 25.1 SQL Dump ('does not dump roles'); pg_dumpall option -g/--globals-only

claims.text: pg_dump does not block other users reading or writing. Operations needing an exclusive lock on a table it reads, such as most forms of ALTER TABLE, wait until the dump ends; while such a request waits, later reads and writes of that table queue behind it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.1 SQL Dump (exceptions: exclusive lock, most forms of ALTER TABLE); pg_dump -j note on queued exclusive lock requests; 13.3.1 Table-Level Locks

claims.text: Dumps of several databases taken one after another each reflect a different moment, so after restoring them together a row in one database (a payment) can reference data (an order) missing from another restored database.
claims.source_hint: Follows from claim 2 (each pg_dump has its own transaction) and backup-logical.sh lines 18-21 (sequential loop); PostgreSQL 17 docs pg_dump

claims.text: With dumps alone, data committed after the last dump is lost if the server is lost, so the RPO is the time between dump runs; dumps kept on the database's machine are lost with it.
claims.source_hint: Course definition of RPO (devops.l3.rpo-and-rto); backup-logical.sh lines 7-8 comment

claims.text: backup-logical.sh lines 7-26 (stage-3) write each run to a new directory in the backups volume (outside db-data, same machine), pg_dump five databases with --format custom one after another, then pg_dumpall --globals-only into globals.sql; output lists 7 files, customers 5.

Outside the excerpt, backup-logical.sh lines 28-43 read orders, order_items and customers back out of donhang.dump with pg_restore, write row counts to counts.txt and print the listing; lines 13-14 leave out lab databases that scripts rebuild.
Keycloak keeps its data (including the realm's signing keys) in the keycloak database on db from stage-3.
To restore a custom-format dump you create an empty database and pass it to pg_restore with --dbname (-d); --table (-t) restores only that table's definition and data, without its indexes.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_restore options -d/--dbname, -t/--table, Examples (createdb then pg_restore -d)

claims.text: A plain copy of a running server's data files (tar and similar) is not a usable backup; the documentation says the server must be shut down for it, because such copies are not atomic and the server buffers changes internally.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.2 File System Level Backup, restriction 1 ('The database server must be shut down in order to get a usable backup')

claims.text: Restoring a dump onto a server where the owning role was never created makes pg_restore report errors that the role does not exist; the dump records ownership but not the role, and the api cannot log in with a role that does not exist.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.1.1 Restoring the Dump ('the users who own the dumped objects ... must already exist'); pg_restore --no-owner

claims.text: Each run of backup-logical.sh names its directory after the second it started (date +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S, mkdir -p), so runs started at different seconds write separate directories.
backup-logical.sh lines 4-5 re-run the script inside the lab box container (lab service), which mounts the backups volume at /backups and reaches PostgreSQL at host db by its service name.
